name.text: RMS Book - Ch1Q3 - Match evidence to methods

questiontext.text:
Mission 3: Build the investigation

The team has a promising research question but wants to start laying out plots immediately.

Drag the five planning decisions into a defensible order. The point is not to memorise a recipe: make the research question determine what evidence and design are needed.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] {#parsons_encode(proof_steps)#} [[/parsons]]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

[[hint title="Planning hint"]]

Begin with what you need to learn, then decide what would count as evidence. Interpretation and limitations come after observations.

[[/hint]]

generalfeedback.text:
Debrief: question before design

One defensible sequence is: identify the gap; specify evidence; design the comparisons; collect outcomes and relevant contextual measurements; interpret the contrasts with limitations.

The precise order of some planning activities can be iterative in real research. This exercise emphasizes the logical dependency between the question and the design, not a rigid administrative timeline.
